title: Thread Spawning for Small Datasets
pattern: Splitting a tiny dataset or trivial task across multiple operating system threads or parallel iterators without measuring the workload size.
why_bad: The overhead of thread creation, OS scheduling, memory allocation, and joining is massive (~10–100 µs) compared to executing a simple loop (~1–10 ns) on a single thread. This results in negative speedup where parallel code runs much slower than optimal sequential code [2, 13, 23, 234].
detection: Spawning threads (`std::thread::spawn`) or using parallel frameworks (such as `rayon` parallel iterators) for loops with a constant, small number of iterations (e.g., < 1000 items) or trivial calculations.
counterexample: The tasks performed in parallel are highly blocking I/O operations (such as fetching 5 distinct web pages) rather than simple calculations. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Process the small dataset sequentially on a single thread.
